items.answer: No contradiction found. Checked the examples against C1 using 0-based indexes (BBB+ = 7, BBB = 8, BBB- = 9, BB+ = 10). BBB+ -> BB+ is 3 steps worse, and with C3's sign (downgrade positive) notchChange('BBB+','BB+') = 3. Likewise BB+ -> BBB+ = -3 and A -> A = 0. The REQ summary gives only magnitudes ('3-notch downgrade'); C3 fixes the sign, so the result is the index of current minus the index of previous. C1 lists exactly 19 ratings, which matches '19 steps'. 'Tests next to the code under test/' is settled by the repo convention test/<area>/<name>.test.mjs, giving test/ratings/notch.test.mjs (CLAUDE.md). Non-string input throws RangeError, not the usual TypeError; C2 states this explicitly, so RangeError is binding.

items.answer: There is one requirement delivered as one card, so there is nothing to prioritise against.

Module src/ratings/notch.mjs (ESM). Named export RATING_SCALE: the 19 ratings in C1 order, best first, as these exact upper-case strings with ASCII '+' and '-': 'AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'. Named export notchChange(previous, current): both arguments must be primitive strings. Each is trimmed with String.prototype.trim() and matched case-insensitively against RATING_SCALE. It returns an integer Number equal to index(current) - index(previous): positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 = unchanged. The range is -18..+18. The function is synchronous and pure. RATING_SCALE's container type/mutability: see X-scale-immutability (pm).
items.quote: `RATING_SCALE` — the 19 ratings of C1, best first. … `notchChange(previous, current)` → integer (C3). … Input is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and case-insensitive … The result is signed: downgrade positive, upgrade negative, unchanged 0.

items.answer: If either argument (previous or current) is invalid, notchChange throws a RangeError. There is no fallback value. Invalid means one of: (a) a non-string: undefined (missing argument), null, number, boolean, object, array, symbol, or a String object such as new String('A'); (b) an empty string; (c) any string that is not one of the 19 C1 ratings after trim() and case-folding. Case (c) includes whitespace-only strings (they trim to ''), ratings outside the scale ('CC','C','D','NR','SD','BBB++'), internal whitespace ('BBB +') and look-alike characters such as the Unicode minus U+2212. The message text is not specified; see X-error-message (pm).
items.quote: Every invalid input (an unknown rating, an empty string, a non-string) is rejected with a RangeError. A String object such as `new String('A')` is a non-string.
